findings.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — `guests.filter(...)` only de-dupes against existing `booking.attendees`, never against the input array itself and the server schema has no `.refine` uniqueness, so a client that skips the UI (or any direct tRPC call) inserts N duplicate Attendee rows for the same email; the only uniqueness guard lives in the browser (confidence 100, P1).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:76 — read-then-write TOCTOU: existence is checked with a prior `SELECT` (`!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`) and there is no unique index on Attendee(bookingId, email), so two concurrent addGuests calls both pass the check and both `createMany`, producing duplicate attendees (confidence 75, P1).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:76 — duplicate detection and blacklist matching use case-sensitive `===` / `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` while the blacklist is lowercased at line 71, so `Bob@x.com` both bypasses the blacklist and is inserted alongside an existing `bob@x.com` attendee (confidence 100, P2).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:46 — `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` requires a user to be BOTH admin and owner (an impossible role pair for admins), so the team-authorization branch is effectively dead and team admins fall through to FORBIDDEN — the intended relation is OR (confidence 100, P1).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:47 — `booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0` and `booking.userId || 0` use `0` as a magic sentinel id for "no team"/"no organizer", turning a missing relation into a real-looking primary-key lookup; the second one makes `findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: 0 } })` throw an unhandled 500 for organizer-less (managed/team) bookings instead of a typed error (confidence 75, P2).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:26 — the handler never inspects `booking.status` or `booking.endTime`, so guests can be added to CANCELLED, REJECTED, PENDING or long-past bookings, and the resulting ICS is emitted with `status: "CONFIRMED"` + `method: "REQUEST"`, resurrecting a cancelled event in the new guest's calendar (confidence 100, P1).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — the attendee rows are committed by `prisma.booking.update` outside any transaction and before `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` (line 165), which is an un-timeboxed sync fan-out to external calendar/video providers with no timeout, retry or compensating rollback; a provider failure leaves the DB with guests the real calendar event never learns about and aborts before any email is sent (confidence 100, P1).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` builds the EventManager from the *acting* user's credentials rather than the booking organizer's, so when an attendee or team admin adds a guest the calendar/video update runs against the wrong (or empty) credential set and silently no-ops (confidence 75, P1).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the raw request array instead of `uniqueGuests`, so emails that were filtered out as duplicates or blacklisted are still classified as "new", and an existing attendee whose address was resubmitted receives a fresh AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the add-guests notice (confidence 100, P2).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:124 — the `evt: CalendarEvent` is hand-assembled and omits `team`, `customInputs`, `responses`, `additionalNotes`, `bookingFields` and `attendeeSeatId`; because `evt.team` is never set, the `if (calendarEvent.team?.members)` branch in sendAddGuestsEmails is unreachable and team members are never notified (confidence 75, P2).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:145 — the handler copies `seatsPerTimeSlot`/`seatsShowAttendees` onto the event but writes Attendee rows directly with `createMany` and never creates the corresponding BookingSeat, so on a seated event type this materializes an attendee with no seat — an illegal state the seats read paths and cancel-seat flow cannot represent (confidence 50, P1).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:138 — `recurringEvent: parseRecurringEvent(...)` is attached to an ICS built from a single booking row, so a guest added to one occurrence of a recurring series receives an invite for the whole series while the DB only records them on that one booking (confidence 50, P2).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:83 — new guests inherit `timeZone` and `locale` copied from the organizer row, redundant derived data stored per-attendee that silently drifts if the organizer later changes locale/timezone and misrepresents the guest's actual timezone in every subsequent email and ICS (confidence 75, P3).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:173 — the mutation returns the untyped hardcoded English literal `{ message: "Guests added" }` and discards which of the submitted addresses were actually inserted vs. dropped as duplicate/blacklisted, so the client unconditionally toasts success and can never surface partial application (confidence 100, P3).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — no BOOKING_UPDATED webhook or workflow trigger is fired after mutating the attendee list, so every downstream integration subscribed to booking changes silently misses guest additions (confidence 50, P2).

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:541 — `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` performs a linear scan of the guest list inside a map over every attendee (O(n*m)) and is case-sensitive, so a guest whose stored address differs in case is mailed the wrong template (confidence 100, P3).

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:549 — `await Promise.all(emailsToSend)` rejects on the first failing recipient and the caller swallows it with a bare `console.log`, so one bad address poisons the batch's error signal and there is no record of which notifications actually went out (confidence 75, P2).

packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts:28 — `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` indexes the attendee array unguarded to build the subject line, throwing on any event with an empty attendee list and rejecting the whole Promise.all batch (confidence 75, P2).

packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:2 — the component imports `{ Button, EmailField, Icon, Tooltip } from "@calcom/ui"`, the same barrel (packages/ui/index.tsx:153) that re-exports it, creating a package-level import cycle that only survives because MultiEmailLazy defers it through `next/dynamic` (confidence 75, P2).

apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26 — a second `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` is defined inline in the component body (rebuilt every render) with stricter rules than the server schema of the identical name in addGuests.schema.ts, so the shared validation contract exists in two divergent copies and the strict one runs only in the browser (confidence 100, P2).

apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:49 — `if (multiEmailValue.length === 0) return;` is dead because the state is initialized and reset to `[""]`, so the empty case instead falls through to the email validator and reports "Emails must be unique and valid" for an untouched form (confidence 100, P3).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:26 — [conf 100][P1] `prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } })` never checks `status`, so guests can be added to CANCELLED/REJECTED/PENDING bookings via a direct tRPC call, emailing "guests added" + a CONFIRMED .ics for an event that is not happening.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:26 — [conf 100][P2] No `endTime`/past-booking guard, and BookingListItem.tsx:554 renders `bookedActions` when `isBookingInPast && isConfirmed`, so "Add guests" is offered on finished meetings and blasts CONFIRMED calendar invites for a past slot.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:46 — [conf 100][P1] `const isTeamAdminOrOwner = (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))` uses AND, so team admins who are not owners are denied despite the variable name and intent; also `booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0` runs both team queries with teamId 0 for every personal booking.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — [conf 100][P2] Duplicate detection is exact-match only (`guest === attendee.email`) and the incoming `guests` array is never de-duplicated server-side, so `["a@b.com","a@b.com"]` or `A@B.com` vs existing `a@b.com` creates duplicate attendee rows and duplicate emails.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:77 — [conf 100][P2] `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` compares a lowercased blacklist against the raw guest string, so any mixed-case blacklisted address bypasses the blacklist entirely.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:138 — [conf 100][P2] For recurring bookings only the single instance is updated while `recurringEvent: parseRecurringEvent(...)` is put on the event, so the emailed .ics describes a whole series while every other occurrence keeps the old attendee list.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:145 — [conf 75][P1] Seated events are unhandled: attendees are created with no `BookingSeat` reference and `seatsPerTimeSlot` capacity is never checked, so adding guests overbooks the slot and produces attendees who cannot cancel/reschedule their seat.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:96 — [conf 100][P2] The attendee rows are committed before `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` (line 165), which is not wrapped in try/catch — a calendar API failure throws after the DB write, so the user sees an error toast, no emails are sent, and the guests are silently already added.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — [conf 75][P3] `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the raw input rather than `uniqueGuests`, so a resubmitted existing attendee is classified as a new guest at email-manager.ts:541 and receives a full "booking scheduled" email for an unchanged booking.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:55 — [conf 100][P3] The FORBIDDEN message key `you_do_not_have_permission` was not added to apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json, so `t(err.message)` in AddGuestsDialog renders the raw key string to the user.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — `const uniqueGuests = guests.filter((guest) => !booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email) && ...)` de-duplicates only against *existing* attendees and never against the incoming array itself, so a payload of `["a@x.com","a@x.com"]` (the server schema `z.array(z.string().email())` has no uniqueness refine, unlike the client's) inserts two Attendee rows for the same person via `createMany`, producing duplicate invites/emails and permanent duplicate rows with no unique constraint and no cleanup path. packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:145 — the handler passes `seatsPerTimeSlot` / `seatsShowAttendees` into the event yet inserts Attendee rows with a bare `createMany` and no corresponding BookingSeat record and no capacity check against `seatsPerTimeSlot`, so on a seated event type the new guests become seat-less orphan attendees that seat-scoped cancel/reschedule flows cannot resolve, and the booking is silently pushed over its seat limit. packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:131 — `booking?.userPrimaryEmail` is read from the Booking model but is the only occurrence of that field anywhere in the repo and the PR adds no migration or schema change, so if the review-base Booking model lacks the column this is schema drift that fails at query/type time (or silently yields `undefined` and mis-addresses the organizer on the calendar event). packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:138 — guests are written to exactly one `bookingId` while the event sent to the calendar carries `recurringEvent: parseRecurringEvent(booking.eventType?.recurringEvent)`, so for a recurring series only a single Booking row gets the new attendees while the calendar update is applied with recurring semantics, permanently desynchronizing the DB attendee lists of the remaining occurrences from the calendar. packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:46 — `const isTeamAdminOrOwner = (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))` uses AND where the name and the "admin or owner" intent require OR, so team admins who are not owners are denied and the effective permission model is narrower than stated (confidence 100, P1).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:52 — `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` grants every attendee the power to mutate the booking's attendee list, a broadening of the permission model beyond organizer/team-admin that the task never sanctioned (confidence 75, P2).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);` passes the raw input rather than `uniqueGuests`, so an address filtered out at line 74 (already an attendee, or blacklisted) is classified as a "new guest" at email-manager.ts:541 and re-sent a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` booking confirmation, altering notification semantics from "guests added" to a duplicate booking notice (confidence 75, P2).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:1 — the task titled "guest management functionality" is delivered as an add-only endpoint (`addGuestsHandler`) with no remove or edit guest path anywhere in the diff, silently narrowing "management" to a single verb without explicit acceptance of the reduced objective (confidence 75, P2).
